title: Skate Parks and Scooter Days: Free Fun on Wheels
description: Skate parks for kids and teens: free ramps for scooters, skateboards and BMX, park etiquette, helmets and pads, and indoor parks for wet days.
intro: Public skate parks are one of the best free days out for kids and teens on scooters, skateboards and BMX bikes. Here’s how to roll in confidently.

image.alt: A skateboarder at a skate park at sunset

cardText: Free ramps, etiquette, safety kit and quiet times.

blocks.title: Scout’s skate park etiquette
blocks.text: Watch before you drop in, take turns and don’t sit on ramps. Early mornings are calmer for beginners and younger kids.
points: Indoor skate parks for rainy days (usually paid)

sections.html: Many councils list skate parks on their websites, and lots are free to use. Indoor skate parks charge, but they’re dry, often have beginner sessions and sometimes offer lessons.

• Wait your turn and watch the flow of riders.
  • Don’t stand or sit in the landing zones.
  • Little ones are safer at quieter times.
A properly fitted helmet is the must-have, plus knee and elbow pads and wrist guards for beginners. More wheels fun in karts, skates and bikes and more free days out.

faqs.a: Many outdoor public skate parks are free. Indoor skate parks usually charge for sessions.
